html: The Taiwano, who call themselves Eduria, are a small Tukanoan-speaking people of the Pirá Paraná region in the Vaupés of south-eastern Colombia. Their language is very close to that of the Barasana. Like their neighbours, they belong to a regional system in which people must marry someone from another language group, so many households use several languages. They live in longhouses (malocas) along the rivers, growing cassava and fishing. In the forests between the rivers live the Yuhup and other hunting peoples.
